bandReport.notes: Band b1 = p00-p07, Q1-56 contiguous with no gaps. Per-page: p00 Q1-8, p01 Q9-15, p02 Q16-22, p03 Q23-30, p04 Q31-39, p05 Q40-45, p06 Q46-51, p07 Q52-56 (rate varies 5-9 per page). Booklet code STS-M-TPT; printed page numbers advance by TWO — (2-A), (4-A), (6-A), (8-A), (10-A), (12-A), (14-A), (16-A) — i.e. only the even printed pages are in the render, the bilingual-booklet parity. Question numbering is nevertheless contiguous across consecutive renders with no gaps, so no page is missing. SEAM CHECK: p07/p08 is CLEAN — p08 opens at Q57 ('A hollow cube is formed by joining six identical squares...'), a standalone question complete on its own page, so nothing of mine spills forward and nothing of b2's reaches back; Q56 is complete on p07. There is no backward seam (p00 is the paper's first question page). NO DIRECTIONS BLOCKS ANYWHERE IN p00-p07 — all 56 questions are standalone, so no question carries context or setLabel. Q45, Q52 and Q53 each print 'Consider the following statements :' but in every case the numbered statements are INTERNAL to that one question, not a shared stimulus over several items, so they are transcribed inside the stem. NO FIGURES in this band: zero of the 56 questions reference a diagram, and every geometry-flavoured item (Q46 triangle sides 5-13-12, Q49 circum-radius, Q53 building and tower, Q54 river bearings, Q56 two circles) is fully stated in words. Raised middle dots: EVERY occurrence in this band is a DECIMAL, never a multiplication or time separator — Q9 (0.83, 0.62), Q10 (12.5, 33.5), Q13 (4.6, 4.8, 5.2, 5.4), Q36 (0.7782, 0.9031, 4.6813, 5.5813, 1.5813, 6.6813), Q45 (1.8, 3.15, 1.35), Q54 (0.5), Q56 (12.5) — all transcribed as full stops per the brief. Rupee glyph printed as the Indian rupee sign in Q26, Q30 and Q43; transcribed 'Rs.' per the corpus convention (no sibling band uses the glyph). RECURRING DECIMALS Q9: the bar sits over the LAST digit ONLY — 0.8 with the bar on the 3, and 0.6 with the bar on the 2 — verified at 4.5x zoom; transcribed \overline{3} and \overline{2}. Without the bars those two values are ordinary terminating decimals, so the bar is load-bearing. TWO MISPRINTS FLAGGED, both preserved as printed and neither repaired: Q23 (the fourth fraction's numerator prints 'b - x^2' while the first prints 'a - x^2', confirmed at 9x — the letter carries a clear ascender) and Q39 ('watcr' for 'water', the glyph confirmed at 9x against the crossbarred 'e' of 'outlet', 'the', 'leaking', 'open' and 'then' on the same and adjacent lines). ONE INVENTED SUBTOPIC: Q54 'Bearings and Horizontal-Plane Observations' — it is a pure horizontal-plane bearing problem (N alpha E / N beta W) and the Heights and Distances chapter lists only elevation/depression and shadow subtopics; no bearings question exists anywhere in the shipped cds-maths corpus. ONE LOOSE FIT flagged: Q31 (roster notation and the empty set) filed under 'Set Operations and Venn Diagrams' following the shipped 2019-1 Q99 precedent. Greek letters transcribed as LaTeX commands throughout (\alpha in Q1/Q52/Q54, \beta in Q54, \theta in Q46/Q48/Q51/Q52, \phi in Q31, \pi in Q47/Q48/Q51). Q55 prints the radian superscript as a literal 'c' (1^c) and is transcribed that way, as the stem itself defines it. Q17 prints 'not' in bold italics; transcribed as **not** per the corpus convention.

questions.stem:
Let AB represent a building of height \(h\) metre with A being its top, B being its bottom. Let \(A'B'\) represent a tower of height \((h + x)\) metre \((x > 0)\) with \(A'\) being its top and \(B'\) being its bottom. Let \(BB' = d\) metre. Let the angle of elevation of \(A'\) as seen from A be \(45^\circ\).

Consider the following statements :

Statement I : \(h + x > d\)
Statement II : The angle of depression of B as seen from \(A'\) is less than \(45^\circ\).

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements ?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true but Statement II is not the correct explanation of Statement I

options.label: C
options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

options.label: D
